ops.title: Bare `log` in the harness shell hits the zsh builtin, silently no-oping unified-log queries — always /usr/bin/log
ops.body:
Bare `log show ...` in the harness Bash tool resolves to zsh's builtin `log` (watch-login), not `/usr/bin/log`. The builtin errors with `(eval):log:1: too many arguments`, and when the call is piped through a filtering `grep` that error is swallowed — the query looks like it legitimately returned zero events.

**Why:** four forensic queries in the 2026-07-14 hostname investigation silently no-oped this way; the tell only surfaced through an inverted (`grep -v`) pipe.

**How to apply:** always write unified-log queries as `/usr/bin/log show ...` / `/usr/bin/log stream ...`. Generalize: when a zero-result comes from a piped system command in this shell, check whether a zsh builtin shadowed it (`echo ===` similarly breaks on zsh's `=cmd` expansion).

Related: [[vmnet-nat-internetsharing]]
